newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade surplus falls to 9.8 bln DM in May.
newsitem.headline: German trade surplus falls to 9.8 bln DM in May.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus in May fell 5.7 percent to 9.8 billion marks, down from 10.4 billion marks the previous month, according to preliminary data from the Federal Statistics Office.
But the total was up 6.5 percent from the year-ago surplus of 9.2 billion marks in May 1996, the office said.

The current account, the broadest measure of trade including services, was in deficit by 2.5 billion marks in May, compared with a surplus of 3.2 billion marks in April and a deficit of 2.9 billion marks a year ago.
Exports in May were 70.8 billion marks, up from the previous month's 73.3 billion marks and the year-ago figure of 64.5 billion marks.

For the first five months of 1997, the trade surplus was 44.6 billion marks, up from 36 billion marks a year earlier, while the current account was in deficit by 7.8 billion marks, growing from a 5.7 billion mark gap a year ago.
Exports in the January-May period totalled 346.8 billion marks, compared to 319.1 billion marks in the first five months of 1996.
